label: checker-b
statement: Reviewed only classifier-contract.md and checker-b-sample.json; no quarantine file was read. No sampled tool supplied an optional analog.

findings.issue: The claimed cross-level return is absent from the named directional information-flow concept.
findings.reason: Central dogma supplies no product-to-instruction return edge; loop depth alone cannot establish a ring.

findings.issue: The parameters implement a bounded replay remedy rather than the named unbounded-replay anti-pattern.
findings.reason: A finite history limit implements bounded replay, not replay without a buffer-size bound.

judgments.reason: Named seek, avoidance and separation weights change the combined acceleration and resulting unit paths.
Separation, cohesion and velocity weights alter neighbour spacing and heading agreement for the flock.
Explicit steering ranks and an acceleration threshold change which group supplies motion and when it switches.
Slot spacing changes fixed target positions, formation width and measurable member-to-slot error.
Spacing, anchor speed and lag limit control moving slot targets and visible anchor-to-member distances.
Travel, danger and visibility costs change selected region costs and therefore route choice and total cost.
Source strength and radius alter the terrain influence field and the resulting controlled or contested areas.
The decay exponent and source strength reshape influence contours and the distance at which control persists.
A finite radius changes which terrain regions receive influence and where the field ends.
A tick delay directly moves notification arrivals later and changes pending notification counts.
Slot spacing and moving-anchor speed change member trajectories, formation error and arrival spread.
Danger and exposure weights alter tactical route costs, producing observable route and risk changes.
A numeric selector threshold directly admits or drops complete unit messages at the channel.
Recipient count changes the numbered delivery set, producing a measurable number of message copies.
The next sequence value and finite buffer control which reordered messages can leave consecutively.
Polling interval and batch limit change pickup times and the number of queued messages received per turn.
Lease duration bounds notification delivery in time while subscriber count changes its recipient set.
The type count defines numbered matching routes, making type-based channel delivery visible.
The stated reciprocal creation relation is a closed represented path; exposed depth changes its visible levels.
Description level switches the visible representation between individual rules and the whole system.
Capture-to-display feedback provides an actual represented return path whose exposed depth can change.
Central dogma does not establish a product-to-instruction return edge; loop depth cannot create that relation.
The specified three creator relations close a represented return path; loop depth controls its exposure.
Description level changes the visible dialogue, narrator or viewer representation directly.
Await-reply and in-flight limits alter sender blocking, queued requests and reply completion timing.
Batch size and flush interval alter how command messages leave the queue and how long they wait.
Subscriber count and notification delay change actual notification recipients and arrival times.
A single active input with completion-gated pending inputs produces sequential, input-ordered message delivery.
The active-input limit changes concurrent routes and pending inputs while open inputs deliver on arrival.
The stated first-emission rule and one-winner limit select one delivery route and close losing inputs.
The sampling period controls delivery ticks for the latest new message and changes delivery count and latency.
Setting delivery delay to zero makes delivery occur in the sending step, directly changing message timing.
The stated first-emission rule and one-winner limit select one delivery route and cancel the others.
A history limit of 1 to 20 implements bounded replay, not the named absence of a buffer-size bound.
The explicit adjacent-equality suppression policy drops repeated payloads and delivers changed values.
The accepted numeric type code filters real message deliveries and counts rejected types.
One in-flight delivery plus FIFO queues writes until completion and preserves delivery order.
Window length and leading/trailing flags directly control immediate, suppressed and boundary deliveries.
A size of seven to nine creates an actual squad membership set; it does not claim to measure effectiveness.
The per-tick message quota changes admitted deliveries and the remaining queue depth.
